newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African police clash with anti-drugs group.
newsitem.headline: South African police clash with anti-drugs group.

text.p: Seven South African policemen have been wounded, two of them seriously, in clashes with militant Moslem anti-drugs campaigners, police said on Tuesday.
They said 24 people in all were in custody after two separate clashes, the first near Cape Town's international airport on Monday and the second outside a courtroom early on Tuesday.

Police spokeswoman Vivienne Phillips said members of the movement People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad) staged an unauthorised protest near the airport against the drugs trade and refused repeated police demands to disperse.
"After the incident outside the airport, 13 Pagad members were arrested and appeared in the Bellville magistrates court later," Phillips said.
She said a crowd gathered outside the court during a bail application on behalf of the arrested Pagad members, abusing police and demanding the release of their friends.
"While police were guarding the building, shots were fired at them from the crowd. Police arrested 11 Pagad members and confiscated five firearms, two illegal and three licensed."
Two policemen were wounded at the airport and five more at the courthouse, she said.
Phillips said eight of the activists would face charges of attempted murder and others would be charged with offences ranging from illegal gathering to hindering the police.
Pagad coordinator Aslam Toefy told Reuters that police had shot protesters without provocation and warned that his supporters could not be expected to turn the other cheek.
Claiming that Pagad members had gone unarmed to the courthouse, he said several of his followers were wounded by police fire.
Pagad came into prominence in August when its members publicly torched and killed a known drug lord and gang leader.
